review.summary: Found one concrete medium-severity issue: the rate limiter's bucket map can grow without bound when it receives high-cardinality traffic during a window. No critical or high-severity finding was established from the supplied diff.

checks.detail: The explanation route checks for the user's session ownership, an attempt, and the in-progress exam restriction before reserving credit. Successful responses include the remaining balance and daily allowance.
The AI router applies requireAuth, validates the explanation request with UUID fields, and checks session ownership before generating an explanation. The panel renders model text as React text nodes.
Generation failures, quota exhaustion, empty output, and provenance logging failures have explicit handling. Generation failures and empty output attempt a credit refund.
The explanation route validates questionId and sessionId as UUIDs. The study-chat route uses studyChatRequestSchema.
Both generation routes use limitAiCalls and the panel handles success, loading, and error states.
No breaking behavior is verifiable from the supplied diff.
The diff provides no tests for the new explanation route, credit reserve/refund paths, rate limiting, or panel behavior, and does not justify their absence.
The limiter's MAX_BUCKETS pruning does not cap the map when all buckets are still active; high-cardinality traffic can make the map grow without bound during the rate-limit window.

findings.title: Active buckets can grow without bound
findings.detail: The sweep only deletes expired buckets. If requests arrive from more than MAX_BUCKETS distinct client IPs while their buckets are still active, the sweep removes none and every new IP adds another entry. Repeated high-cardinality traffic can therefore grow the per-process map without a cap, increasing memory use despite the MAX_BUCKETS constant.
findings.suggestion: Enforce a hard capacity for active buckets, or use a bounded store/eviction strategy that preserves the intended rate-limit behavior under high-cardinality traffic.
